title: Project health: CI proves the build, robustness at the edges, painless onboarding
description:
Findings from a whole-repository audit (Rust crates, web app, Python analysis, CI, release, docs).

Purpose: make CI prove what the project already claims, harden the FFI and browser audio edges, and let a new contributor get a first sound out of a clean checkout on any platform.

Definition of done: every child issue closed; CI builds the wasm crate, runs every existing test suite (Rust, wasm, web, Cucumber, pytest), and enforces rustfmt and clippy; a Linux checkout builds by following the README alone.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text:
Suggested order, highest leverage first:

1. CI runs everything that already exists: wasm build and tests (apricitus-1f0e91), Cucumber conformance (apricitus-e83164), pytest/ruff/mypy (apricitus-8f7022), rustfmt/clippy/doc/audit (apricitus-2698fb).
2. A clean Linux checkout builds from the README alone (apricitus-d4fbd5); Python packaging declares its imports (apricitus-ae920d).
3. Split the compiler and parser (apricitus-6372d1), then structured compile errors (apricitus-38a9a4).
4. Harden the edges: wasm FFI (apricitus-205813), analysis server (apricitus-fca129), browser audio failure paths (apricitus-5cb893).
5. License text and the Swift licensing decision (apricitus-94da2e); release version bumps (apricitus-7edd75).

Everything else on this epic is independent and can be picked up in any order.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text:
Correction to the order above: three IDs were wrong.

- Step 2, one-command setup on Linux: apricitus-446dba (not d4fbd5, which is the typed Amplify client and lint issue).
- Step 5, license text and the Swift licensing decision: apricitus-874f56 (not 94da2e, which is the Playwright smoke test).
- Step 5, release version bumps: apricitus-b799ab (not 7edd75, which is keyboard focus and labels).
